title: Perf Canary — Baseline Results (Week 1) — staging + prod-shadow
content:
Perf Canary — Baseline Results (Week 1)
Owner: Nadia Rahman
Last updated: 2026-02-18

Context
- Goal of this sheet: capture initial baseline distributions for p50/p95/p99 latency + tokens/sec (and component breakdowns) from staging and prod-shadow canary runs.
- Intended usage: seed baseline store + draft first-pass regression thresholds (warn/page) for phase-1 (us-east) rollout.
- Notes:
  - These are NOT customer-traffic numbers. This is synthetic prompt distribution v0 (shape-only) and controlled run scheduling.
  - “prod-shadow” here means canary hitting internal inference endpoints in the production environment but gated to low QPS + non-customer prompts.
  - Week 1 showed higher-than-expected variance in a couple buckets; see “Variance / caveats” section before turning on paging.

Run configuration (Week 1)
- Date range: 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-17 (inclusive)
- Regions covered: us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1 (limited smoke), us-west-2 (staging only)
- Hardware SKUs sampled:
  - H100-SXM-80GB (Dedicated + Hosted pools)
  - A100-80GB (legacy pool)
  - L40S-48GB (staging only)
- Runtime build(s): rw-runtime 2026.02.11-rc2 (majority), 2026.02.13-rc1 (partial overlap due to deploy)
- Canary QPS cap: 0.15 QPS/model/SKU (target <0.5% GPU overhead). Burst disabled.
- Workload profile: canary-prompt-set-v0
  - Prompt length buckets (approx tokens): 128, 512, 2k, 6k
  - Decode target: 128 tokens (with a small 512-token tail)
  - Mix: 40% short (128), 35% medium (512), 20% long (2k), 5% extra-long (6k)
  - Request mode: streaming ON
  - Temperature 0.2, top_p 0.9 (fixed)
- Metrics definitions:
  - e2e_latency_ms: request start -> last token
  - runtime_latency_ms: runtime admission -> last token
  - queueing_ms: scheduler queue wait (runtime-exported)
  - prefill_ms: prefill/TTFT-ish (runtime-exported)
  - decode_ms: decode portion (runtime-exported)
  - tokens_per_sec: generated tokens / (runtime decode time); also record e2e_tps as generated tokens / e2e time (more noisy)

Quick summary (what we learned)
1) H100 baselines are stable enough for warn-level alerts with modest dampening; A100 needs wider thresholds or SKU-specific baselines.
2) Queueing time is the dominant driver of p95 variance during peak-hour background load even at low canary QPS. Execution-only metrics (runtime_latency_ms w/ queueing removed) are materially more stable.
3) For Llama-3 70B on H100, tokens/sec is low-variance; for Mixtral, tokens/sec shows more variance tied to batch size distribution shifts.
4) Telemetry ingestion lag (2–6 min bursts) created “sawtooth” in per-minute p95 when querying raw series. Recommend baselines and alert queries use 10m windows minimum for now.

=== TABLE C: Variance and stability (prod-shadow us-east-1) ===
This table is intended to guide alert dampening + minimum sample sizes.

Definitions
- CV(p95): coefficient of variation of the p95 across 10m windows (stddev/mean)
- “Peak hour delta”: mean p95 during 16:00–21:00 UTC minus mean p95 during 02:00–07:00 UTC
- “Queue contribution”: fraction of e2e p95 attributable to queueing p95 (approx)

| Model (canonical)                    | SKU            | CV(e2e p95) | CV(runtime p95) | Peak hour delta (e2e p95) | Queue contribution @p95 | Interpretation |
|--------------------------------------|----------------|-------------|-----------------|----------------------------|------------------------|----------------|
| llama-3-70b-instruct@3.0             | H100-SXM-80GB  | 0.08        | 0.04            | +220 ms                    | ~10–15%                | runtime stable; e2e driven by queue tail |
| mixtral-8x7b-instruct@0.1            | H100-SXM-80GB  | 0.11        | 0.06            | +180 ms                    | ~12–18%                | tps variance correlates with batch_p95 shifts |
| qwen2.5-32b-instruct@2.5             | H100-SXM-80GB  | 0.09        | 0.05            | +200 ms                    | ~12–16%                | stable enough for warn; watch for baseline drift |
| llama-3-70b-instruct@3.0             | A100-80GB      | 0.16        | 0.11            | +540 ms                    | ~18–25%                | too noisy for tight thresholds; needs SKU baselines |


Observations / caveats (Week 1)
1) Queueing metrics are “bursty” and can dominate e2e p95 with small background shifts.
   - Recommendation: alert primarily on runtime_latency_ms p95 AND queueing_ms p95 as separate signals (two panels), rather than only e2e.
   - For gating releases: use runtime p95 as hard gate; use queueing p95 as informational unless we confirm scheduler change.

2) Tokens/sec for Mixtral is more sensitive to batch size distribution.
   - In windows where batch_p95 dropped from ~18 -> ~12, we saw ~8–12% tps degradation with no meaningful change in runtime p95.
   - Hypothesis: batcher heuristics + competing traffic shifts micro-batch composition.
   - Recommendation: include batch_p50/p95 panel and treat tps regressions as “throughput” regressions even if latency is unchanged.

3) Telemetry ingestion lag affected high-resolution queries.
   - Grafana panels at 1m resolution produced artifacts (flatlines then bursts).
   - Recommendation: baselines computed over 10m windows, alerts evaluate over 15m windows with min_samples.

4) Kernel tag stability
   - For H100, kernel tag was stable (attn_v4.3) for Llama/Qwen; for A100 we saw occasional fallback to attn_v4.0 during one deploy window.
   - Recommendation: do not roll A100 into phase-1 paging until kernel-selection tag is fully reliable (or force kernel in config during baseline building).

5) KV cache hit rate is effectively ~0 in this workload.
   - Expected due to high prompt diversity and no intentional prefix repetition.
   - Decision needed: if we want KV cache regression coverage, we need a second synthetic profile with controlled prefix reuse.


Draft baseline + threshold suggestions (not final; for discussion)
These are intentionally conservative to avoid Week-1 false positives.

Proposed minimum sample sizes (per model/region/SKU)
- Warning-level evaluation: >= 200 requests AND >= 12x 10m windows in last 2h
- Paging-level evaluation (top models only): >= 500 requests AND >= 24x 10m windows in last 4h

Proposed deviation thresholds (relative to baseline median of p95 over last 7d)
- runtime_latency_ms p95
  - Warn: +8% sustained for 30m
  - Page (top models): +15% sustained for 45m
- tokens_per_sec p50
  - Warn: -10% sustained for 30m
  - Page (top models): -18% sustained for 45m
- queueing_ms p95
  - Warn: +25% sustained for 30m (informational / triage)
  - Page: only if coupled with runtime p95 +15% OR correlated with scheduler deploy

Suggested “top model” initial paging candidates (phase 1)
- llama-3-70b-instruct@3.0 (H100, us-east-1)
- mixtral-8x7b-instruct@0.1 (H100, us-east-1)

Suggested “warn-only” initial candidates
- qwen2.5-32b-instruct@2.5 (H100, us-east-1)
- All A100 SKUs until we have stable kernel tag + SKU-specific baselines for >=2 weeks


Open questions / TODO (Week 2)
- [Noah] Decide whether baseline store should be keyed by (model, runtime build, kernel tag, SKU, region) or whether kernel tag is recorded as attribute only.
- [Rina] Add a second canary profile with prefix reuse to validate KV cache hit-rate instrumentation + regressions.
- [Logan/Nadia] Confirm ingestion lag root cause and whether we can reduce p95 artifacts; otherwise enforce 10m aggregation in canned queries.
- [Aisha] Convert threshold suggestions into SLO-toolkit templates and align warn/page policy with SRE.
- [Omar] Validate queueing_ms semantics under load (ensure it excludes client-side retries / admission control time).

Appendix: Notes on data hygiene
- Canary prompts are synthetic and do not include customer inputs.
- We should avoid adding high-cardinality labels (full prompt bucket id, request id, full kernel name). Current plan: bucketed prompt_len, bucketed decode_len, kernel_tag (coarse), model_id (canonical), model_version, runtime_build, region, sku, pool_tier.

Changelog
- 2026-02-12: initial sheet created; imported first 48h prod-shadow stats (H100 only).
- 2026-02-15: added A100 baselines + variance table; added telemetry lag caveat.
- 2026-02-18: updated numbers after extending window to full week; added draft thresholds + min-samples guidance.
